context: Daichi explains how long fishing takes to catch a fish.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ダイチおじさん、いつ、お魚、来る？
lines.en: Daichi-uncle, when will the fish come?
lines.style: Soft, earnest question with genuine curiosity. Small voice but steady. A pause before 'when' as if checking he's asking the right thing. Warmth threading underneath.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 時間、かかるで。じっくり待つ。
lines.en: It'll take a little while, you know. Just wait patiently with me.
lines.style: Warm Kansai lilt on the rhythm. Patient and encouraging without rushing him. Real affection in the slower beat. The regional swing loose and easy throughout.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Small, serious commitment. No false brightness—he means it. Quiet determination in a six-year-old's voice. Slight lift at the end, like he's making a promise to himself and to Daichi both.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 一緒に、釣り、楽しいやん。
lines.en: Fishing together is fun, isn't it?
lines.style: Warm and inviting, with the Kansai swing. Speaking not just to convince Sho but to marvel with him. Genuine pleasure in the moment, not performing it. A small man's quiet generosity.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: I'll remember my first time fishing.
lines.style: Small voice, but weight to it. He's making a mental note, fixing this in memory. Soft certainty—not bragging, just knowing this matters. Barely-audible warmth at the very end.
